description: A NON-button control (a select, colour picker, grid picker, toggle or dropdown) that can leave a TmToolbar Overflow=Menu bar like a TmToolbarButton. The wrapper is the measured item: it collapses whole (out of flow, invisible, inert) and its width stays measurable. In the More menu the item is offered as plain menu entries — one entry (MenuLabel + OnMenuInvoke) or a labelled group (MenuItems); a free template inside role=menu is invalid ARIA, so a host action typically opens the full control in a dialog or sheet (MenuKeepOpen). A TmDropdown or TmSplitButton inside a TmToolbar joins the roving tab stop automatically; other custom focusables can be wrapped in a TmToolbarItem.

parameters.name: ChildContent
parameters.description: The control rendered on the bar (a TmSelect, TmColorPicker, TmToggle, TmDropdown, …).

parameters.name: Priority
parameters.description: How important the item is when its TmToolbar runs out of room (ToolbarOverflow.Menu). An overflow rank only — items render in written order. An item collapses only when it offers something in More: MenuItems with entries, or a non-empty MenuLabel bound to an OnMenuInvoke handler; without either it has no menu representation and never leaves the bar (it behaves as ToolbarButtonPriority.Pinned whatever this value is).

parameters.name: MenuLabel
parameters.description: The label of the item's More entry (or, with MenuItems, the header and accessible name of its group). With an OnMenuInvoke handler it makes the item collapsible; without one (and without MenuItems) the item never leaves the bar.

parameters.name: MenuIcon
parameters.description: Optional icon of the single More entry (an IconNames value). Ignored with MenuItems.

parameters.name: OnMenuInvoke
parameters.description: Runs when the user picks the item's single More entry. Typically opens the full control in a dialog or sheet (then set MenuKeepOpen). Invoked exactly once per activation. Together with a non-empty MenuLabel it makes the item collapsible; a label without a handler (and without MenuItems) never leaves the bar. Ignored with MenuItems.

parameters.name: MenuKeepOpen
parameters.description: Maps to TmActionItem.KeepMenuOpen for the single entry: the menu stays open while the surface the action opens is shown (it paints above the menu).

parameters.name: MenuItems
parameters.description: Instead of one entry, offer these entries in More, rendered as one labelled group (MenuLabel) in the given order — e.g. the sizes of a font-size select as checkable entries (TmActionItem.Checked). Each entry's Group and GroupLabel are overwritten by this item; every entry needs a unique Id (or a unique Label — the label is the fallback key the menu dedupes and focuses by). The list is compared structurally when the toolbar decides whether to recompute: a fresh-but-equal list per render is not a change, so a host may rebuild it whenever the rendered state changes.

parameters.name: Disabled
parameters.description: Disables the More entry (or every MenuItems entry). The bar control's own disabled state stays the host's: set both.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class for the wrapper element.

examples.title: Font-size select collapsing into More as a labelled group
examples.code:
<TmToolbar Overflow="ToolbarOverflow.Menu" AriaLabel="Text tools">
    <TmToolbarItem MenuLabel="Font size" Priority="ToolbarButtonPriority.Secondary" MenuItems="@_fontSizes">
        <TmSelect TValue="int" Value="@_fontSize" ValueChanged="@OnFontSize" Options="@_fontSizeOptions" />
    </TmToolbarItem>
    <TmToolbarButton Icon="save" Text="Save" />
</TmToolbar>

@code {
    private readonly IReadOnlyList<TmActionItem> _fontSizes = new[] { 8, 10, 12, 14, 18 }
        .Select(s => new TmActionItem { Label = s.ToString(), Checked = _fontSize == s ? true : null,
            OnClick = EventCallback.Factory.Create(this, () => _fontSize = s) })
        .ToList();
}

examples.title: Colour picker offered as one entry that opens a dialog (menu stays open)
examples.code:
<TmToolbarItem MenuLabel="Text colour" Priority="ToolbarButtonPriority.Secondary"
             OnMenuInvoke="@OpenColourDialog" MenuKeepOpen="true">
    <TmColorPicker @bind-Value="_textColour" Placeholder="Text colour" />
</TmToolbarItem>
